2014|website=USAB.com|access-date=August 11, 2016}} is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Marinos B.B.C.|Marinos de Anzoátegui]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (SPB). He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]] before being drafted 40th overall in the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. ==High school career== Stone attended [[Dominican High School (Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin)|Dominican High School]] in [[Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin]]. As a senior, he averaged 24.4 points and 11.7 rebounds per game. He finished his career with 2,193 points.{{cite web|first=JR|last=Radcliffe|url=http://archive.whitefishbaynow.com/sports/dominicans-diamond-stone-left-a-mark-that-will-be-remembered-for-decades-b99474580z1-299046571.html|title=Dominican's Diamond Stone left a mark that will be remembered for decades|work=WhiteFishBay.com|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=April 8, 2015}} During his four years, he helped lead Dominican to four-straight WIAA Division 4 state championships.{{cite web|first=Jim|last=Polzin|url=http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/badgers-men-s-basketball-uw-loses-out-to-maryland-in/article_c1a75fe4-4b6d-5956-903e-0c915b809da3.html|title=Badgers men's basketball: UW loses out to Maryland in Diamond Stone sweepstakes|work=Madison.com|date=March 28, 2015|access-date=March 28, 2015}} During the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015 McDonald's All-American Game]], Stone hit 7-of-9 shots for 14 points and also had three rebounds.{{cite web|first=Roman|last=Stubbs|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/terrapins-insider/wp/2015/04/01/maryland-commit-diamond-stone-scores-14-points-in-mcdonalds-all-american-game/|title=Maryland commit American Game, sparking NCAA title talk|work=BaltimoreSun.com|date=April 2, 2015|access-date=April 2, 2015}} A five-star recruit coming out of high school,{{cite Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] in March 2015,{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Stewart|url=http://archive.jsonline.com/sports/preps/diamond-stone-chooses-maryland-b99470549z1-297856071.html|title=Diamond Stone chooses Maryland|work=JSOnline.com|date=March 27, 2015|access-date=March 27, 2015}} and signed with the program in April.{{cite web|first=Don|last=Markus|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2015/04/15/diamond-stone-signs-agreement-to-join-terps/|title=Diamond Stone signs agreement to join Terps|work=BaltimoreSun.com|date=April 15, 2015|access-date=April 15, 2015}} ==College career== Diamond Stone signed with Maryland. Stone averaged 12.5 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.6 blocks in his lone season at Maryland. Named AP Big Ten Newcomer of the Year, he established the Maryland freshman record and all-time XFinity Center mark with 39 points against [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]] on December 30, 2015.{{cite web|url=http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=29700&ATCLID=210607587|title=STONE SCORES 39, LEADS #4 TERPS PAST PENN STATE|work=UMTerps.com|date=December 30, 2015|access-date=December 30, 2015|archive-date=February 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160224055751/http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=29700&ATCLID=210607587|url-status=dead}} On April 11, 2016, Stone declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility. He was later selected with the 40th overall pick in the 2016 NBA Draft.{{cite web|first=Don|last=Markus|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2016/04/11/marylands-melo-trimble-diamond-stone-to-declare-for-nba-draft-stone-to-hire-agent/|title=Maryland's Melo Trimble, Diamond Stone to declare for NBA draft; Stone to hire agent|work=BaltimoreSun.com|date=April 11, 2016|access-date=April 11, 2016}} ===College statistics=== Diamond Stone averaged 12 points, 5 rebounds, and 0.4 assists on 56% shooting efficiency. Also, he averaged 2.7 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Diamond Stone College Stats {{!}} Sports Reference |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/diamond-stone-1.html |website=Sports Reference |access-date=September 13, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2016–2017)=== On June 23, 2016, Stone was selected by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] with the 40th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/draft2016/story/_/id/16398364/2016-nba-draft-new-orleans-pelicans-pick-diamond-stone-maryland-center-no-40-overall|title=Pelicans pick Diamond Stone, Maryland center, at No. 40 overall|work=ESPN.com|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=December 4, 2016}} He was later traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on draft night.{{cite web|first=Rowan|last=Kavner|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-trade-rights-michineau-stone/|title=Clippers Trade For Rights To Michineau, Stone|work=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=June 23, 2016}} On July 14, 2016, he signed with the Clippers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-diamond-stone|title=CLIPPERS SIGN DIAMOND STONE|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2016|access-date=July 14, 2016}} Stone played only 24 minutes for the Clippers in his rookie season, but showed promise on both ends of the floor during his time in the [[NBA Development League]];{{cite web|last=Agar-Johnson|first=Nicholas|url=http://hoopshabit.com/2017/05/06/los-angeles-clippers-2016-17-report-cards-diamond-stone/|title=Los Angeles Clippers 2016-17 report cards: Diamond Stone|work=HoopsHabit.com|date=May 6, 2017|access-date=July 4, 2017}} he had multiple [[assignment (NBA D-League)|assignments]] with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] and [[Salt Lake City Stars]], pursuant to the flexible assignment rule.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 4, 2017|archive-date=June 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628000000/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/|url-status=dead}} === Windy City Bulls and Salt Lake City Stars (2017–2018) === On July 6, 2017, Stone was acquired by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in a three-team trade involving the Clippers and the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-first-round-pick-diamond-stone-and-jamal-crawford|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire First-Round Pick, Diamond Stone and Jamal Crawford|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2017|access-date=July 6, 2017}} On July 31, 2017, he was waived by the Hawks.{{cite web|last=Vivlamore|first=Chris|url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/basketball/hawks-waive-diamond-stone/Lul0pCfZQWrLe2vi5cg9CN/|title=Hawks waive Diamond Stone|work=AJC.com|date=July 31, 2017|access-date=July 31, 2017}} On September 14, 2017, he signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-diamond-stone|title=BULLS SIGN DIAMOND STONE|work=NBA.com|date=September 14, 2017|access-date=September 14, 2017}} He was waived by the Bulls on October 16, 2017.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-jarell-eddie-and-diamond-stone-claim-kay-felder|title=BULLS WAIVE JARELL EDDIE AND DIAMOND STONE, CLAIM KAY FELDER|work=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2017|access-date=October 16, 2017}} Stone started the season playing for the [[Windy City Bulls]], and was traded to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] for [[Henry Sims]]'s rights and a third-round 2018 pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/865695135/SLC-Stars-trade-for-a-Diamond-Stone.html|title=SLC Stars trade for a Diamond Stone|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=January 17, 2018|access-date=July 2, 2018}}{{dead link|date=November 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} === Iowa Wolves (2018–2019) === Stone played in the summer leagues for the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/maryland/article/diamond-stone-finds-summer-league-home-119464903/|title=Stone Finds Summer League Home|work=247sports.com|date=June 29, 2018|access-date=July 2, 2018}} On November 14, 2018, the [[Iowa Wolves]] acquired the returning right to Stone from the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] in exchange for the returning player right to [[Wes Washpun]] and a third-round draft pick in the 2019 NBA G League Draft.{{cite web|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-acquire-returning-player-rights-to-diamond-stone-in-trade-with-salt-lake-city/|first=Seth|last=Nutting|title=Wolves Acquire Returning Player Rights to Diamond Stone in Trade with Salt Lake City|date=November 14, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 14, 2018}} Later on November 26, 2018, the [[Iowa Wolves]] announced that they had acquired Stone,{{cite web|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-acquire-diamond-stone/|first=Seth|last=Nutting|title=Wolves Acquire Diamond Stone|date=November 26, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}} but was later waived by the [[Iowa Wolves]] on January 4, 2019.{{cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/iowa-wolves-waive-diamond-stone/|title=Iowa Wolves waive Diamond
